title: QB1_A#q13 taught sewage sludge as still on the London Protocol's Annex 1 permitted list after Resolution LP.6(17) removed it
candidate_claim: Transcribed from the Founder's correction brief, not the reporter's own words (the original message and screenshots are not held in this repository): CE Oral Tip on Q13 reads 'Sewage sludge: on the permitted list under 1996 Protocol (subject to conditions)'; sewage sludge was subsequently removed from Annex 1 of the London Protocol.
authority: PRIMARY. (1) Resolution LP.6(17), adopted 7 October 2022 by the Seventeenth Meeting of Contracting Parties to the 1996 Protocol, Annex: Annex 1 paragraph 1 'Delete sub-paragraph 1.2 ... .2 sewage sludge; Renumber the subsequent sub-paragraphs'; consequential deletion in Annex 2 paragraph 4; operative: 'Contracting Parties shall not issue new permits for dumping of sewage sludge after the entry into force of the amendment' and active permits may be maintained 'until the expiry date, but not later than 31 May 2027'. Registered as SRC-IMO-LP6-17. (2) Status of IMO Treaties Vol. II, 30 September 2026, LC PROT 1996 (3) 2022 amendments: entered into force 15 January 2023 under Article 22.4 except for Canada, Finland and China, whose objections were later withdrawn (Canada 29 Nov 2023; China 17 Apr 2025, not Macao SAR unless notified; Finland from 1 Oct 2025); LC PROT 1996 has 56 Contracting States, LC 1972 has 87. Registered as SRC-IMO-STATUS-TREATIES-VOL2-2026-09-30. (3) 1996 Protocol Article 22.4 (IMO consolidated text). All read 2026-10-28.
rationale: The CE Oral Tip stated the pre-2023 position as current, and two further limbs of the same card - the reverse-list paragraph and the 60-second answer - listed sewage sludge among the Annex 1 permitted materials, so correcting the tip alone would have left the card contradicting itself (miw-correction-workflow SKILL.md 'Scope creep' and 2a). All three limbs are corrected; the reg-box gains the LP.6(17) row; the CE Oral Tip carries the examiner cross-question; version v1.0 -> v1.1. The corrected text states the amendment's legal scope (binds Contracting Parties to the 1996 Protocol; not States party only to the 1972 Convention) and separates it from MARPOL Annex IV, so it is not taught as an unconditional worldwide ban.
